entrypoints.summary: A first external-provider federated signup invokes the PreSignUp_ExternalProvider guard with a Cognito federated username containing the provider and attacker-controlled subject.
PostConfirmation_ConfirmSignUp consumes the same federated username after confirmation and derives custom:primaryEmail from its subject portion.

affected_components.role: PreSignUp_ExternalProvider uniqueness guard parses subject token index 1.
PostConfirmation consumer parses the final subject token and writes custom:primaryEmail.
Application authorization oracle for staff and organization-admin roles.

code_slices.surrounding_context: The configured lab uses Cognito user-pool infrastructure and Lambda functions; the web application applies staff_required to /admin and org_admin_required to /directory.
code_slices.vulnerable: The PreSignUp handler selects sub.split("_")[1] for its list_users uniqueness filter, while the PostConfirmation JIT handler selects sub.split("_")[-1] and writes it as custom:primaryEmail.

negative_controls: A session role other than staff receives the Staff-only area access-denied response.
A role outside staff and org-admin receives the organization-admin access-denied response.
observability.positive_marker: The protected /admin route renders only after staff_required accepts a session role of staff.

preconditions: A deployment accepts federated external-provider signup and reaches both the described pre-signup and post-confirmation handlers.
An attacker can provide a subject with an extra underscore-delimited middle segment.
The final subject segment is a staff-recognized email value and the guard's second segment does not collide.

trigger_steps.summary: Federate through the external provider with an underscore-bearing subject whose second and final tokens differ.
Allow the later JIT handler to store the final subject token as custom:primaryEmail.

capabilities.concept: differential parsing of federated identity subject

impacts.concept: privilege escalation to staff-protected application functions

The research post identifies pre-signup as the pre-persistence gate, while the code demonstrates the inconsistent parsing that a single canonical validation path must eliminate.

impact.affected_asset: Staff-only administration and staff-or-org-admin application functionality, including the /admin and /directory authorization boundaries.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause a federated identity to be persisted with a staff-recognized primary-email value despite the uniqueness guard checking a different subject fragment.
impact.security_effect: Authorization identity collision / privilege escalation in the lab application

causal_trace.summary: An external OIDC identity can supply a subject with extra underscores, such as EVIL_noise_support@acme.org, embedded after the provider prefix in the federated username.

The pre-signup uniqueness guard interprets the second underscore-delimited subject token as the identity to check, whereas the later JIT consumer interprets the final token as the canonical primary email; thus the checked identity is not necessarily the identity persisted for authorization.
After confirmation, the JIT Lambda appends the final subject token as custom:primaryEmail and writes it with the Cognito administrative user-attribute update API.

The JIT code identifies custom:primaryEmail as an attribute the application uses to recognize platform staff, while the application exposes staff-only /admin and staff-or-org-admin routes; a crafted primary email can therefore create staff authorization meaning in the intentionally vulnerable lab configuration.

failure.operation: admin_update_user_attributes persists custom:primaryEmail derived from the final underscore-delimited subject token after a guard checked a different token.

primary_invariant.statement: The identity value checked for cross-IdP uniqueness must be the same unambiguous identity value later persisted as custom:primaryEmail and consumed for authorization.
primary_invariant.violated_because: Two trigger handlers independently split the attacker-controlled subject on underscores using different positional rules: the guard selects index 1 and the JIT consumer selects the last token.

quality.review_notes: Primary code artifacts directly document the parser differential and administrative attribute write. The bundle contains deployment instructions and authorization-route code, but no captured end-to-end execution trace proving that a crafted subject reached a privileged route. This is an intentionally vulnerable lab/configuration pattern, not evidence of an AWS Cognito product defect. No fixed implementation or patch commit is supplied.

remediation.invariant_restored: Before the federated user record is created, validate the same canonical provider/subject-derived identity that downstream provisioning will persist; avoid positional delimiter parsing of an attacker-controlled subject and do not derive security-sensitive authorization identity from differently parsed input.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The attacker controls an external federated OIDC subject containing multiple underscore-separated segments.
data_structure_invariants: The provider-prefixed username has a subject portion.
The canonical authorization identity must not vary by which handler parses the same subject.
state_context.state_machine: First federated sign-in reaches the pre-signup gate before local-user creation, then post-confirmation provisioning; later authorization uses attributes persisted on the Cognito user.

target.component: AWS Cognito federated-signup triggers and Random Cats Extractor application authorization
